survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is an ICILS 2013 technical report describing the study’s complex sampling design and the computation of sampling and nonresponse weights for student, teacher, and school data. It specifies that all international reporting in ICILS is based on weighted data, using final student weights (e.g., TOTWGTS) and final teacher weights (e.g., TOTWGTT) that combine base selection probabilities with nonresponse adjustments across explicit strata. It also describes replicate-weight generation (jackknife repeated replication) for variance estimation, and participation-rate adjudication rules (e.g., discarding schools with <50% within-school response). Because this is a framework/technical documentation chapter rather than an empirical ML analysis paper, the report does not provide an analytic model that applies these weights to a predictive target; however, it clearly instructs secondary analysts to use the provided weights and replicate weights when estimating population quantities and standard errors.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because the document is a technical report describing assessment construction, scaling, and sampling/weighting procedures rather than reporting an empirical predictive analysis with a PV-based dependent variable. The report does discuss PV methodology for deriving CIL achievement statistics, but it does not present a student-level ML model with a PV outcome and therefore does not document PV handling in the sense required for an empirical ML extraction. Missing-data handling is not reported in the ML sense because no ML model is estimated; instead, the report provides general guidance on data cleaning, scaling, and participation requirements.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: ICILS 2013 targets students in Grade 8 (or Grade 9 in Norway) with mean age at least 13.5 years, and teachers teaching regular subjects to the target grade. The analytic sample is restricted by (i) school exclusions (e.g., very small/special-needs schools and other nationally defined exclusions), (ii) within-sample student exclusions (e.g., students with disabilities or insufficient test-language proficiency), and (iii) within-school participation requirements: a school is included as a participating school in the student survey only if at least 50% of sampled students participated (responded to at least one test task). Additional exclusions occur when survey operation procedures were not properly followed (e.g., incomplete listing/coverage), and participation categories determine whether countries’ results are annotated or omitted from international reporting.

data.outcome_summary: ICILS 2013 is a computer-based large-scale assessment of computer and information literacy (CIL) for lower-secondary students (target grade typically Grade 8; Norway used Grade 9). The student test comprised four 30-minute modules with two modules administered per student via a balanced complete rotation, and the CIL scale was derived using a Rasch model with proficiency levels and achievement statistics produced through plausible value methodology with full conditioning. The study used a stratified two-stage cluster sampling design: PPS systematic sampling of schools followed by systematic stratified sampling of students and teachers within schools, with explicit and implicit stratification variables varying by country. To support valid population inference, the report specifies final sampling weights that combine base selection probabilities and nonresponse adjustments, and it describes replicate-weight logic (jackknife repeated replication) for sampling variance estimation. It also documents stringent participation-rate and within-school response thresholds (e.g., discarding schools with <50% within-school response) to reduce bias from nonresponse and operational deviations.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for an official IEA technical report describing ICILS 2013 instruments, scaling, sampling, translation/verification, and weighting/variance-estimation procedures. The document does not present an empirical ML prediction/classification analysis with a defined dependent variable and reported model performance; therefore, fields such as total_students, ML techniques, and main findings are not populated beyond the assessment-design and weighting specifications. The sparse ML-related fields are a consequence of the report’s purpose (technical documentation rather than an ML study), not an omission of empirical results.
